name: Pay a fee online through the gateway from the parent app
priorityReason: The only route that does not need a family to travel or an office to key anything.

goal.capability: to pay my child's outstanding fee from the app
goal.outcome: the bill is settled without a trip to the bank, and the school sees it immediately

secondaryActors.involvement: Sees the payment recorded and reconciles the settlement later.
Reviews the payment and attempt log.
May pay their own outstanding invoice where the school permits it.

externalActors.involvement: Processes the transaction and returns whether it succeeded or failed. Holds no login.

additional.description: The gateway returns its result, which decides whether a payment is recorded.

preconditions.condition: An issued invoice exists with an outstanding balance.

establishedBy.name: Issuing fee invoices at different scopes

preconditions.condition: The guardian is signed in to the parent app and the invoice belongs to their own child.
A payment gateway is configured and live for the branch. Setting it up is not part of this use case.
The gateway is reachable. Where it is not, the invoice simply stays payable by the other routes.

postConditions: On success the payment is recorded against the invoice and a numbered receipt has been issued, through the same path as any other payment.
The invoice reads Paid or Partially paid, and has left overdue tracking where it is settled.
The gateway's transaction reference is held against the payment, which is what reconciliation matches on later.
On failure the invoice is untouched and still outstanding, and the attempt is logged with the gateway's reason.
A guardian is never charged without the invoice being credited, and the invoice is never credited without the gateway confirming.
The settlement has not yet been reconciled against the bank. Money confirmed by a gateway is not the same as money in the school's account.
The attempt log holds every try, successful or not, so a family saying they paid can be checked.

dataFields.validation: Issued before the guardian leaves for the gateway, so an attempt exists even if they never come back (BR-5).

entities.notes: One per try, successful or not. Never deleted (BR-9).
Read for the outstanding balance; its status moves only on a confirmed success.
Created on success through the ordinary payment path, not by a separate route (BR-2).
Issued on success by the same path as any other payment.

permissions.notes: Initiates the payment. Cannot see any other family's invoice or attempt.
May pay where the school permits it.
Sees payments and attempts, and reconciles the settlement later. Does not initiate an online payment on a family's behalf (BR-10).

permissions.rowScope: Own branch; may switch per branch-scope.
permissions.notes: Reviews the payment and attempt log.

businessRules.rule: An invoice is marked paid only on a confirmation the gateway returned. Nothing is credited because the guardian says they paid, or because the browser came back.
A successful payment is recorded through the ordinary payment path, so an online payment produces the same numbered receipt and the same ledger postings as a payment made at the counter.
The amount defaults to the full outstanding balance. Where a part payment is permitted, the invoice reads Partially paid and the balance stays outstanding.
An amount greater than the outstanding balance is refused before the guardian reaches the gateway. It is easier to refuse than to refund.
An attempt reference is issued before the guardian leaves for the gateway. Without it a payment made by a family who never returns to the app cannot be tied to an invoice.
The gateway's transaction reference is held against the payment. It is what reconciliation matches on when the settlement reaches the bank.
A failure is shown to the guardian in the gateway's own terms, so they know whether to try again or use another card. The invoice stays outstanding and is untouched.
An attempt left pending past the configured window is queried against the gateway and resolved. A payment is never left in limbo because a callback was lost.
Every attempt is logged, successful or not, so a family saying they paid can be checked against what actually happened.
Accounts do not initiate an online payment on a family's behalf. The guardian's own act is what authorises the charge.
A repeated confirmation for the same transaction reference records the payment once. A gateway retrying its callback must not credit an invoice twice.
Confirmation by the gateway is not the same as money in the school's account. The settlement is reconciled separately, and until then the payment is recorded but unreconciled.

transitions.condition: The guardian is directed to the gateway.
No result within the configured window, and the query finds no transaction (BR-8).
A later query finds the transaction did succeed after all.

basicFlow.userAction: Opens the outstanding invoice for their child.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Shows the invoice and its outstanding balance, for their own child only.

basicFlow.navigation: My children's fees → Pay invoice → Payment method
basicFlow.systemResponse: Checks the amount is not more than the outstanding balance before the guardian goes anywhere.
Creates the attempt with its reference and directs the guardian to the gateway.

basicFlow.userAction: Completes the payment on the gateway.

basicFlow.systemResponse: Returns whether the transaction succeeded or failed, with its transaction reference.
On success, records the payment through the ordinary payment path, which issues the numbered receipt and posts to both ledgers.
Shows the guardian the receipt on success, or the gateway's reason on failure with the invoice still outstanding.

alternateFlows.navigation: Gateway → Payment result → My children's fees
alternateFlows.behaviour: The invoice is untouched and still outstanding. The guardian is shown the gateway's reason so they know whether to try again or use another method, and the attempt is logged (BR-7, BR-9).

alternateFlows.condition: The guardian abandons the payment at the gateway
alternateFlows.behaviour: The attempt is closed as cancelled, the invoice is untouched, and no charge was made.

alternateFlows.condition: The guardian pays but never returns to the app
alternateFlows.behaviour: The gateway's callback resolves the attempt, and the attempt reference issued at step 3 ties the payment to the invoice. The receipt is sent to the guardian without their coming back (BR-5).

alternateFlows.condition: No result arrives within the configured window
alternateFlows.navigation: Fee → Online payment attempts → Query gateway
alternateFlows.behaviour: The attempt is queried against the gateway and resolved either way, so a payment is never left in limbo because a callback was lost (BR-8).

alternateFlows.condition: The gateway sends the same confirmation twice
alternateFlows.behaviour: The transaction reference is recognised and the payment is recorded once. An invoice is never credited twice for one transaction (BR-11).

alternateFlows.condition: The guardian pays part of the balance
alternateFlows.behaviour: The invoice reads Partially paid afterwards and the balance stays outstanding and payable by any route (BR-3).

exceptions.condition: The amount exceeds the outstanding balance
exceptions.systemResponse: The guardian is not sent to the gateway (BR-4).
exceptions.messageShown: The outstanding balance is PKR 4,000. Enter that or less.

exceptions.condition: The invoice has already been paid
exceptions.messageShown: This fee has already been paid.

exceptions.condition: The invoice belongs to a child who is not theirs
exceptions.systemResponse: It does not open, per role-based-access.
exceptions.messageShown: You do not have permission to view this record.

exceptions.systemResponse: No attempt is created and the invoice is untouched. It stays payable at the bank or the office.
exceptions.messageShown: Online payment is unavailable at the moment. You can pay at the bank using the challan, or at the school office.

exceptions.condition: The gateway returns a result for an unknown attempt reference
exceptions.systemResponse: Nothing is credited. The result is logged for Accounts to investigate.

exceptions.condition: The ledger posting fails after the gateway confirmed
exceptions.systemResponse: The payment is not lost. The attempt stays Succeeded and unposted, and is flagged to Accounts, because the family has been charged.
exceptions.messageShown: Your payment went through and the school has been notified. Your receipt will follow shortly.

exceptions.condition: The gateway confirms an amount different from the one requested
exceptions.systemResponse: The confirmed amount is recorded and the difference is flagged to Accounts rather than being assumed away.

exceptions.condition: The branch has no gateway configured
exceptions.systemResponse: The pay option is not offered at all.
exceptions.messageShown: Online payment is not available. Pay at the bank using the challan, or at the school office.

departures.requirement: A gateway callback is processed within 5 seconds and is safe to receive more than once, since gateways retry.
An attempt is never left unresolved. Where no result arrives, the gateway is queried rather than the outcome assumed.
No card or bank detail ever reaches this system. The guardian enters them on the gateway, and only a transaction reference comes back.
The whole flow works on a 360 px phone screen, since almost every guardian will pay from one.

conventionsApplied.name: session-and-authentication
conventionsApplied.rule: Every use case except the login use case assumes an authenticated session. Sign out is available on every screen. An expired or invalid session returns the user to the login screen with the message "Your session has ended. Please sign in again."

conventionsApplied.name: role-based-access
conventionsApplied.rule: Access is enforced server-side on every request, not only by hiding menu items. A request for a record outside the actor's permitted scope returns a 403 and the message "You do not have permission to view this record." A use case states additions and restrictions only.

conventionsApplied.name: branch-scope
conventionsApplied.rule: Every record carries a branch ID. Users see only their own branch unless the use case states otherwise. Super Admin, School Admin and Principal may switch branch from the header.

conventionsApplied.name: academic-session-scope
conventionsApplied.rule: Every academic record carries an academic session ID. Lists default to the current open session.

conventionsApplied.name: list-screens
conventionsApplied.rule: Every list supports search, column sort and page-size selection. Default page size 25; default sort is most recent first. Filters are applied before printing or exporting.

conventionsApplied.name: audit-trail
conventionsApplied.rule: Every create, update, deactivation, approval and reversal writes to the audit log: actor, role, timestamp, record type, record ID, before and after values, and IP address. Audit entries are never editable.

conventionsApplied.name: validation-and-messages
conventionsApplied.rule: Field-level errors appear inline beneath the field on blur and on submit. Errors that block the whole action appear as a banner at the top of the form. Successful actions show a toast. No action succeeds silently.

conventionsApplied.name: money
conventionsApplied.rule: All monetary values are stored as fixed-point decimals in the smallest currency unit, never as floating point. Displayed as PKR with a thousands separator and two decimal places. Rounding is half-up at the line.

conventionsApplied.name: dates-times-numbers
conventionsApplied.rule: Dates display as DD-MM-YYYY; date and time as DD-MM-YYYY HH:mm in 24-hour form. Times are school-local. Phone numbers are stored in the registered mobile format.

conventionsApplied.name: language
conventionsApplied.rule: All user-visible strings come from a resource file. No hard-coded text in any screen.

conventionsApplied.name: concurrency-and-locking
conventionsApplied.rule: Last write wins, except where a use case defines an approval lock. Once a record is approved, posted or issued it becomes read-only and can only be changed through its defined reversal use case.

conventionsApplied.name: screen-states
conventionsApplied.rule: Every list, dashboard tile and report defines four states: loading, empty, error and populated. The empty state names what is missing and links to the action that creates it.

conventionsApplied.name: notifications
conventionsApplied.rule: All outbound SMS, WhatsApp, email and push messages are sent through the Messaging module, recorded in the sent-message log with per-channel delivery status, and use a named template. Use cases reference the template; they do not embed message text.

conventionsApplied.name: default-performance-and-retention
conventionsApplied.rule: Unless a use case states otherwise: a screen loads within 2 seconds and a save completes within 2 seconds at 200 concurrent users; lists paginate above 100 rows; financial and student records are retained 7 years; audit and message logs 12 months; every screen is usable at a 360 px viewport. Fill the non-functional field only to depart from this.

conventionsApplied.name: default-trigger
conventionsApplied.rule: Unless a use case states otherwise, the trigger is: the user navigates to the screen and initiates the action. Fill the Triggers field only where a scheduled job, an event in another module, or an inbound external call also starts it.
